clues: This city stands on the north shore of the River Tagus, in the far west of Europe. The wide ocean waits just past the river mouth.
Winters here are mild and rainy, while summers run warm and dry. The ocean near by and a high air mass keep the weather tame.
In 1255, this city took the top job from Coimbra. It has been the land's capital ever since that year.
Old trams have rolled through this city since 1873, and most cars on the lines are old ones kept in service. Six lines still run today.
Portugal's government sits in this city, and its top court sits here too. The head of state lives here as well.
